statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Egyptian Commercial Registry Portal (Gafeti System, Ministry of Trade and Industry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must primarily appear in Arabic script; Latin transliteration permitted but Arabic prevails; industry-specific names require prior approval
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical or confusingly similar to existing registered entities without consent
Religious or sectarian terms without ministerial approval
Words implying public monopoly or government control
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File administrative appeal to the Minister of Trade and Industry within 15 days of rejection notice; subsequent review by relevant department

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for standard LLCs; virtual offices routinely accepted and compliant within free zones such as the Suez Canal Economic Zone
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium; routine unannounced inspections by commercial registry and tax authorities for substance verification

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 on Companies (as amended by Investment Law No. 72 of 2017); Articles 20-34 on Limited Liability Companies; implementing Ministerial Resolutions; Labor Law No. 12 of 2003.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – One-Stop Shop, with final registration at the Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Contract of Incorporation (Articles of Association) in Arabic, notarized and submitted via the GAFI One-Stop Shop.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLCs under Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 72 of 2017. Capital is determined in the Articles of Association and fully subscribed at incorporation; paid-up funds may remain in a corporate bank account evidenced by a bank certificate. No escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that each subscriber's share subscription to the stated capital of the Company, as set forth in the Articles of Association, be and is hereby ratified and accepted, with paid-up amounts to be deposited in the Company's bank account; RESOLVED, that the registered office address of the Company at [address in Cairo] be and is hereby adopted as its legal seat for all business and statutory purposes; RESOLVED, that the natural persons named in the Articles of Association are appointed as the first managers of the Company, with authority to act singly in executing documents, opening bank accounts, and engaging professional advisors to complete the Company's statutory and licensing obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Corporate Charter Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS), Commercial Registry window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed Arabic company names to the GAFI OSS; obtain an official name reservation certificate after checking availability and compliance with commercial names rules; prepare the draft Articles of Association in Arabic from the GAFI template.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form (GAFI)
Copy of national ID for Egyptian subscribers or passport for non-resident subscribers
Letter of authorization to a local legal agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Refile with alternative names; correct any Arabic transliteration or spelling errors and reapply within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office under the Ministry of Justice; licensed corporate bank in Egypt
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Take the final Articles of Association to a licensed notary public for execution and notarization; open a temporary corporate bank account in the company name and deposit the subscribed paid-up capital; obtain a bank deposit certificate naming all subscribers.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association signed by all subscribers
Name reservation certificate
Passport/national ID copies of all subscribers
Power of attorney, if signed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any notarial defect or missing signature; renotarize after correction; if bank refuses the temporary account, choose another licensed bank and reissue the deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI One-Stop Shop Submission and Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed incorporation dossier to the GAFI One-Stop Shop; pay the official registration fees; receive the corporate incorporation certificate, the commercial registration certificate, and the company's national number in one integrated process.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Articles of Association
Bank deposit certificate evidencing paid-up capital
Name reservation certificate
Lease or usufruct contract for the registered office (or address declaration)
Subscribers' declarations on fiduciary status and disqualifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query, submit the corrected documentation within 15 working days; appeal any refusal to the GAFI internal legal committee if the query is not curable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Tax Card Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) via GAFI OSS post-incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the incorporation certificate, apply for the tax card and registration for income tax, withholding tax, and value-added tax (if applicable); receive the tax identification number (TIN) and official tax card.
required_dossiers: Incorporation certificate and commercial registration certificate
Notarized Articles of Association
Registered office lease contract
Passport/national ID copies of managers and shareholders
Bank account statement or certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide a written response to the ETA's request for clarification; add any missing annexes and resubmit online or at the ETA service window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Manpower and Immigration – General Department of Manpower Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a standalone application for the executive search/headhunting license under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003; include the completed incorporation documentation, workplace safety clearance, and civil defense fire certificate; pay the licensing fee and obtain the operating license.
required_dossiers: Application form for private employment agency license
Commercial registration certificate and tax card
Notarized Articles of Association
Lease contract for the operational office
Civil Defense fire safety certificate
Certificate of social insurance registration for the designated manager
Police clearances for the manager(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license application is refused or queried, correct the specified compliance gaps and reapply; if refusal persists, file an administrative appeal to the Ministry of Manpower's Labor Disputes Committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Industrial Development (non-applicable for office-based service activity; primary sectoral clearance is issued by the Ministry of Manpower and Immigration).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Private Employment Agency (Executive Search and Headhunting) License under Law No. 12 of 2003 and its Executive Regulations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – Registration / Exempt: office-based headhunting and executive search have no industrial installation; no full EIA report required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to non-manufacturing office operations; general compliance with municipal wastewater discharge standards under Law No. 93 of 1962 and solid waste management under Law No. 38 of 1967.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Civil Defense Department of the Ministry of Interior for the registered office; structural load and fire-load inspection certificate from the municipal authority; occupational safety and health clearance from the Manpower Directorate under Law No. 12 of 2003.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Egypt Ministry of Finance; e-Tax portal at www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing and e-receipt system at einvoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must first register with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) to obtain incorporation approval and commercial registration. The LLC must then file an ETA Tax ID issuance application (Tax Card form) through the e-Tax portal within 30 days of commercial registration, submitting the company contract (MOA), commercial registration certificate, board resolutions, legal attorney appointment, office lease proof, passports of managers/owners and financial year data. The ETA issues a unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and a Tax Card showing the VAT, withholding tax and stamp tax registrations. Non-resident owners are not required to obtain a separate TIN for the LLC; a non-resident entity with Egyptian-source income is registered only when a withholding obligation or permanent establishment is identified. VAT registration is mandatory once annual taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed EGP 500,000.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Egyptian tax law. A resident Egyptian LLC is a per se taxable entity subject to corporate income tax on worldwide income; there is no shareholder-level pass-through. Limited special regimes are available by election or by license under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, including the Free Zone regime (subject to ETA/GAFI approval), Special Economic Zones under Law No. 83 of 2002, and certain investment incentives; these do not convert an LLC into a pass-through entity. No hybrid mismatch entity election is recognized in Egyptian domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and amendments, supplemented by generalized e-invoicing and e-receipt regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover threshold for VAT registration; mandatory ETA Tax Card registration applies from the commencement of the LLC's business activity regardless of turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt has a mandatory real-time e-invoicing and e-receipt regime administered by the ETA. B2B and B2G invoices must be transmitted in structured XML or JSON via ETA-approved APIs, cleared in real time, and stamped with a unique QR digital stamp before issuance. The e-receipt system is progressively mandated for B2C transactions, including executive search and headhunting services. All zero-rated export invoices must also be submitted through the e-invoicing system with the appropriate export VAT code. Noncompliance with e-invoicing, e-receipt, or digital stamping rules triggers fines, invoice rejection, and enhanced audit risk.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services consumed outside Egypt qualify for 0% VAT. For executive search and headhunting services, the following criteria are audited: the service is supplied to a non-resident client not registered under the Egyptian VAT law; the service is performed for purposes of the client's business outside Egypt; the benefit, use, and placement result occur outside Egypt; and payment is received in freely convertible foreign currency through a licensed Egyptian bank. The LLC must maintain transparent evidence linking the invoice to an actual offshore service and must reflect the export zero-rating in the e-invoicing system.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration and export manifest for physical goods (not applicable to pure service exports, but required when headhunting transactions include bundled goods or promotional materials)
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or equivalent transport document for physical goods (not required for pure executive search services)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement issued by a CBE-authorized bank confirming receipt of the export proceeds in foreign currency
Executed executive search/headhunting service agreement with the non-resident client, including scope, fee structure and jurisdiction
ETA e-invoice with the zero-rated export code and QR digital stamp evidencing real-time fiscal clearance
Documented service performance evidence: candidate search, interview coordination, placement acceptance, timesheets and final placement reports
Bank wire via retainer or Wise B2B record showing the foreign payer matched to the invoice and the legally required foreign exchange repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA and the Egyptian Central Bank actively audit export zero-rating claims. A claim will be clawed back if the foreign proceeds are not repatriated or evidenced within the applicable period, if the service is found to be consumed in Egypt, or if documentation is missing. Penalties include retrospective VAT assessment at 14%, late-payment interest (currently 2% per month or part thereof, with minimum penalties), financial fines of up to EGP 5 million, and criminal sanctions for tax evasion under Law No. 206 of 2020. In serious cases, the tax evasion offense is punishable by imprisonment, disqualification from GAFI benefits, and nullification of export incentives.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) – Foreign Exchange Administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a generally convertible regime for current account transactions under the CBE Banking Law and Law No. 194 of 2020, while capital account operations require documentary support, bank verification and tax/regulatory clearance. For the EG_LLC executive-search business, service fees received from non-resident clients are current account items and may be remitted abroad after AML/KYC verification, applicable withholding of Egypt corporate income tax and participant tax compliance. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation to non-resident shareholders are permitted under the Investment Law and CBE foreign-investment regulations provided the LLC submits audited financial statements, settles all taxes, and obtains the relevant CBE investment attestation. Practical hurdles arise mainly from hard-currency liquidity in the Egyptian banking market, documentary delays in CBE reporting and periodic manual review of large inbound foreign receipts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Service compensation earned from non-resident clients constitutes service export revenue for Egyptian foreign-exchange purposes. In accordance with CBE regulatory guidance, the full amount of such service export proceeds must be repatriated to Egypt through a licensed bank within 90 days from the invoice date or, if later, final delivery of the executive-search service. A mandatory conversion ratio of 15% of each service-export receipt applies by default; that portion must be converted to Egyptian pounds at the prevailing interbank rate, and the remaining 85% may be retained in the LLC's foreign-currency account for approved transactional purposes. The CBE may allow a lower conversion ratio or a temporary waiver upon documented hedging, reinvestment or financing needs.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for peripheral collections only. Offshore digital EMI services such as Wise and Payoneer are not licensed by the CBE to open EGP-denominated business accounts, effect domestic clearing in Egypt, or provide statutory account evidence for Egyptian corporate tax and FX filings. Such EMIs may be used as an auxiliary collection channel for low-value initial retainers in hard currency, but the EG_LLC must route all statutory-exposure settlement, export proceeds and shareholder distributions through a CBE-licensed bank. Legal constraint: under the Egyptian Banking Law, an onshore entity's business treasury and outward payments must be conducted through an authorized Egyptian bank; foreign EMI balances do not benefit from Egyptian depositor protection or CBE oversight.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory. CBE AML regulations and Egyptian Law No. 80 of 2002 on combating money laundering require banks to conduct face-to-face identification of each corporate account signatory and beneficial owner. Remote/video-based onboarding for foreign-owned LLCs is not generally accepted unless a prior banking relationship exists and the bank approves a limited digital pathway under CBE guidance. At least one managing director, or an appointee holding a notarized power of attorney, must appear in person at the selected bank branch with original incorporation documents, board resolutions, UBO passport copies and tax identification documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Indirect or opaque ultimate beneficial ownership for a foreign-owned Egyptian LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and memorandum of association of all chain entities, up-to-date commercial register extracts, full UBO organogram, passport copies of all owners, notarized beneficial-ownership declaration, source-of-wealth statement for each shareholder, and proof of legal address for each corporate layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound retainer wire transfers originating from a third-party payer or a digital EMI rather than the client entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed retainer agreement and statement of work, final commercial invoice, board resolution from the remitting client identifying the payer, KYC due-diligence memorandum on the ultimate beneficiary, bank reference letter or EMI compliance statement, and contract-linked payment purpose explanation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening flags arising from an executive-search candidate's employer jurisdiction or a recruiting client's ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions screening output against OFAC, EU and CBE lists, explicit intermediary attestation that the ultimate client and candidate are not sanctioned, negative media-review notes, client end-beneficiary questionnaire, and an AML compliance officer memo recommending continued onboarding subject to enhanced monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent large foreign-currency conversions creating apparent FX-trader activity instead of ordinary service settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved cash-flow forecast tied to retainer milestones, sub-agent payment schedule, payroll plan, matching processed MT103 messages or bank debit advisories, explanatory account narrative, and a documented liquidity policy showing that conversions correspond only to operating requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax residence and economic-substance mismatch between the Egyptian LLC and management conducted abroad.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Egyptian tax identification card, VAT registration, lease or usufruct deed for Egypt office premises, local payroll records, signed board-meeting minutes held in Egypt, annual audited financial statements, and utility/telecom invoices evidencing actual business operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: A foreign parent or shareholder capital injection must be transmitted through a CBE-licensed bank using SWIFT MT103 with the clear purpose code for FDI equity participation and a reference to the LLC's foreign-currency account. The remitting bank must include the full legal name, UBO identification where required, and a payment narrative referencing the Articles of Association and board resolution approving the contribution. The receiving Egyptian bank will perform sanctions screening, AML KYC verification, and CBE investor-registration checks, then issue an inward remittance advice and credit the proceeds to the LLC's foreign-currency account. If the injection is made in Egyptian pounds directly, the transfer should use the same FDI purpose code and the bank should complete CBE inward investment reporting so that future dividend repatriation is legitimate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operating trade settlements under executive-search contracts, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 bank-to-bank payment against a valid commercial invoice and retainer agreement. For domestic payments to subcontractors and placement consultants, CBE-cleared EGP transfers or EGP account-to-account credits are appropriate. Commercial letters of credit should not be used for intangible headhunting services; they are only relevant if the LLC imports physical recruitment or IT hardware, in which case a documentary LC requires full import documentation, shipping evidence, and CBE-form-specific review. For hard-currency outgoing payments to foreign network partners, the SGD must be sent from a foreign-currency account through the licensed Egyptian bank with a copy of the underlying engagement contract and invoice to support the transaction purpose.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with a CBE-licensed bank, evidenced by a retainer obligation, quote of fees, or signed sub-agent contract
FX swaps used to align the timing of foreign-currency retainer receipts and sub-agent disbursements where the bank recognizes an underlying commercial exposure
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps only when matched to an existing foreign-denominated borrowing or equity-injection liability
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be used solely as an overlay hedge against hard-currency depreciation risk on confirmed receivables, subject to CBE approval and documented trade exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 19) with audited financial statements attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – electronic filing via tax.gov.eg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of the fiscal year-end; calendar-year taxpayer files by 30 April. Attach audited FS, tax reconciliation and payroll summaries.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EGP 500–2,000 (approx. USD 10–40) for late filing; 2% monthly surcharge on unpaid tax; enforced bank seizure after demand; criminal liability for fraudulent returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Assembly approval of audited financial statements and filing of the signed statements and minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry at GAFI One-Stop Shop; copy to ETA with the CIT return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary General Assembly must approve the audited financial statements within 6 months of the fiscal year-end; minutes and signed audited FS lodged at the Commercial Registry immediately after approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory fine of EGP 1,000–10,000 for non-holding of the annual assembly; GAFI may block commercial-registry extracts and, after 3 years of non-compliance, initiate administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Social Insurance aggregate salary declaration and monthly contribution settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly contribution return and payment due by the 15th of the following month; annual aggregate insured-salary statement due by 31 March after the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% monthly late-payment interest on overdue contributions; NOSI collection order and offset against company VAT refunds; criminal sanctions for knowingly under-declared payroll.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal commercial license / activity occupancy fee and periodic Commercial Registry renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local municipal licensing office and Commercial Registry at GAFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Municipal license occupancy fee payable in January of each calendar year (or within 30 days of invoice); full commercial registration renewal every 5 years from the date of registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Admin fines of EGP 100–500 and suspension of official extracts used for customs clearance, banking and tender qualification; continued default risks premises closure order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of UBO register and shareholder records at the Ordinary General Assembly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office records; available for inspection by GAFI, ETA and AML supervisory authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: UBO and share-quota transfer register updated within 30 days of any change; formal review and confirmation of the beneficial ownership register at the annual assembly within 6 months of year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML Law 80/2002 fines of EGP 50,000–200,000 for deficient or unwarranted refusal of UBO data; false declarations carry criminal penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for all Egyptian LLCs regardless of size; the annual general assembly must appoint a certified Egyptian auditor (registered with the Ministry of Finance/ETA and the certified accountants’ register in Egypt). No turnover exemption under Companies Law 159/1981. Small taxpayers may use the simplified SME tax regime of Law 152/2020 for tax computation but still need audited statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), aligned with IFRS; full IFRS only for listed companies and financial institutions supervised by the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Egyptian LLC must record its ultimate beneficial owners in an internal UBO register under AML Law 80/2002 (Art. 18) and its executive regulations; documentation of UBO identification (ID, no. of shares/quota, source of funds) must be kept with the statutory books. Any share-transfer or quota-cession triggering UBO change must be recorded in the quota transfer register and notified to the register within 30 days; the full register is reviewed and confirmed annually at the Ordinary General Assembly. Companies Law 159/1981 requires LLC quota transfers to be approved and recorded before the transfer is opposable to the company and third parties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (قيد الشركاء) with capital quota details
General Assembly and Manager minute book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% of net taxable profits under the Egyptian Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic sector-specific corporate income tax holiday applies to an ordinary Egyptian LLC conducting executive search or specialist recruitment. Conditional Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 incentives may apply to qualifying new investment projects, including a deduction from taxable investment costs of up to 50% in designated Sector A areas or 30% in designated Sector B areas, subject to statutory eligibility, project approval, documentation, timing, and aggregate incentive limitations. Free-zone treatment is conditional and generally does not cover ordinary domestic-market service activity without specific approval.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual corporate income tax return for legal persons, commonly identified as Form 29 or the corresponding legal-person income tax return in the Egyptian Tax Authority electronic filing portal. Filing is made through the ETA e-tax platform using the taxpayer's tax registration credentials and applicable electronic signature or authentication process.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and tax payment are generally due within four months after the end of the financial year. For a calendar-year company, the ordinary deadline is 30 April of the following year. A company using an approved non-calendar financial year must apply the four-month rule by reference to its own year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax registration number, legal name, legal form, registered address, tax office, activity code, contact details, and return period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or parent is not substituted for the Egyptian LLC. Report the Egyptian LLC's own tax registration details and disclose non-resident ownership and related-party relationships where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial year beginning and ending dates, original or amended return status, and cessation or commencement indicators.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the period approved for the Egyptian entity. A branch, permanent establishment, or other Egyptian taxable presence must file for its Egyptian accounting period even if the foreign enterprise uses a different year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss derived from the approved financial statements before Egyptian income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only the Egyptian entity's accounts. Allocate Egyptian-source income and expenses to an Egyptian permanent establishment using supportable accounting and attribution principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible taxes, penalties, unsupported expenses, personal expenditure, provisions not meeting statutory requirements, excessive or unsubstantiated management charges, and other accounting expenses disallowed for tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to a foreign parent or affiliate require contracts, invoices, evidence of receipt, business purpose, withholding-tax analysis, and transfer-pricing support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permitted business expenses, depreciation adjustments, bad-debt deductions, statutory deductions, and other adjustments required to reconcile accounting profit to taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibility depends on Egyptian business purpose, actual incurrence, accounting support, statutory limitations, and payment or withholding compliance where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax depreciation and adjustments for the difference between accounting depreciation and statutory tax depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Egyptian tax depreciation rules and retain fixed-asset registers, acquisition invoices, import records, commissioning evidence, and ownership documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of transactions with related Egyptian or foreign parties, including services, royalties, loans, guarantees, cost allocations, recruitment-platform charges, and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all material related-party dealings and reconcile the amounts to the general ledger, statutory accounts, withholding returns, and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Any adjustment required to bring related-party transactions to the arm's-length result under Egyptian transfer-pricing rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct a foreign affiliate charge merely because it appears in an intercompany agreement. Demonstrate benefit, actual performance, arm's-length pricing, and Egyptian tax deductibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible tax losses from prior periods carried forward within the statutory five-year period, subject to continuity, substantiation, and applicable limitations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain period-by-period loss schedules and supporting returns. A change in ownership or business activity may require additional review before losses are used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after statutory adjustments, allowable deductions, carried-forward losses, and approved incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Egyptian-source and Egyptian-attributable taxable profits. Do not exclude revenue because the customer, parent, or payment account is outside Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the applicable 22.5% corporate income tax rate, less legally available credits or incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty relief or foreign-tax-credit treatment only where statutory conditions, supporting certificates, and relevant treaty provisions are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax withheld, paid, and balance payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayments, withholding-tax credits, prior payments, approved tax credits, balance due, or refundable amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the return to payment receipts, withholding certificates, payroll and contractor withholding filings, and bank records. Foreign taxes are not automatically creditable without Egyptian statutory support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Audited or otherwise required financial statements, tax reconciliation, trial balance, fixed-asset schedule, loss schedule, related-party schedules, and other ETA attachments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Arabic or officially accepted translated documents where required and preserve the foreign parent agreement, beneficial-owner information, and ultimate ownership chain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized representative declaration that the return is complete and accurate, followed by electronic submission and retention of the filing acknowledgement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian legal representative remains responsible for proper authorization, filing credentials, supporting records, and timely correction of material errors.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing may trigger administrative penalties under the Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 206 of 2020, generally including monetary penalties that increase for repeated or serious failures. Failure to submit a required return may attract a penalty commonly ranging from approximately EGP 3,000 to EGP 50,000, with higher penalties for repeated violations or specified serious breaches. Late payment attracts additional tax calculated under the statutory late-payment formula, generally linked to the Central Bank credit and discount rate plus the statutory margin and calculated by month or part of a month; it is not normally expressed as a simple fixed daily surcharge. Material understatement, concealment, false records, or deliberate tax evasion can create criminal exposure in addition to tax, interest, and administrative penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends distributed by an Egyptian resident company are generally subject to 10% withholding tax. A 5% rate may apply to qualifying dividends related to listed shares or listed securities under the applicable statutory conditions. Treaty rates may reduce the rate where the recipient qualifies as the beneficial owner and all procedural requirements are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the non-resident recipient for the relevant period, verify the applicable Egypt double-tax treaty, beneficial ownership, minimum shareholding or holding-period conditions, limitation-on-benefits requirements where relevant, and any required tax authority documentation. Apply the treaty rate only where the payer can substantiate entitlement. Retain the residence certificate, treaty analysis, ownership records, payment evidence, board or shareholder resolutions, contracts, and withholding filings. If the certificate or treaty entitlement is unavailable at payment, withhold at the domestic rate and pursue any permitted refund or adjustment procedure through the Egyptian Tax Authority. Treaty relief is not created merely by routing funds through a treaty jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Egyptian domestic withholding tax generally applies at 20% to interest, royalties, and certain other payments to non-residents, subject to statutory characterization and exemptions. Applicable tax treaties may reduce the rate, commonly to treaty-specific limits that differ by recipient, payment type, and ownership conditions. Interest paid to a non-resident lender, royalties for intellectual property, software, know-how, trademarks, or similar rights require separate source, treaty, beneficial-ownership, permanent-establishment, and transfer-pricing analysis. Treaty relief requires a valid tax residence certificate and satisfaction of the relevant treaty conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Egyptian transfer-pricing documentation requirements generally apply where related-party transactions exceed the applicable ETA threshold. The commonly applied threshold for Local File documentation is EGP 8 million per related-party transaction category during the relevant fiscal year, subject to the current executive regulations and ETA guidance. A Master File and Country-by-Country Report may additionally be required for Egyptian members of multinational enterprise groups meeting the applicable consolidated-revenue threshold, commonly associated with EGP 3 billion or its prescribed equivalent for the reporting group. Thresholds, filing dates, and format requirements must be verified for the relevant tax year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a standalone United Arab Emirates-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Nevertheless, substance is relevant under transfer-pricing rules, anti-avoidance principles, beneficial-ownership analysis, permanent-establishment rules, deductibility provisions, and treaty application. An executive-search LLC should maintain Egyptian management authority, personnel or demonstrable operational capacity, client and candidate records, office or suitable operating infrastructure, local decision-making, bank and accounting controls, contracts, evidence of service delivery, and commercially rational intercompany arrangements. A company with no meaningful functions, assets, risks, or local decision-making may face denial of deductions, transfer-pricing adjustments, treaty-relief denial, permanent-establishment recharacterization, or sham-transaction allegations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing recruitment revenue, omitting retained search fees, issuing false invoices, maintaining parallel books, fabricating candidate or client expenses, understating taxable profit, or knowingly submitting materially false tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid tax, additional tax, interest, administrative penalties, and potential criminal prosecution under the Egyptian Income Tax Law and Unified Tax Procedures Law. Tax-evasion offenses may result in imprisonment and fines, with the amount depending on the offense, tax loss, repetition, and judicial findings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers, authorized signatories, accountants, and other responsible persons may incur personal criminal liability where they participated in, directed, approved, or knowingly facilitated the violation. Civil recovery may include unpaid tax, penalties, interest, and restitution. Travel restrictions or asset measures may be imposed through applicable judicial or enforcement procedures; they are not automatic merely because a person is a director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without tax registration, failing to file the annual corporate return, failing to update the tax file, or continuing activity after cessation without notifying the tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines for non-registration, non-filing, inaccurate registration data, or late filing; tax assessment based on available information; late-payment additional tax; and possible escalation for repeated or deliberate conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative may be personally exposed to statutory penalties for acts or omissions attributable to the representative. Directors do not automatically become liable for all company tax debts solely by holding office, but personal exposure increases where there is consent, participation, fraud, obstruction, or failure to comply with a specific legal duty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, technical services, or other cross-border amounts without determining Egyptian withholding-tax obligations, without withholding, or without remitting and reporting tax on time.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the tax that should have been withheld, additional tax and interest, filing penalties, and potential penalties for inaccurate or missing withholding returns. The payer may bear the economic cost if it failed to deduct the tax from the payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Authorized representatives and responsible finance personnel may face personal liability where the failure was deliberate, fraudulent, or specifically attributable to them. Treaty documents obtained after payment may not automatically cure an earlier failure to withhold.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting Egyptian search profits to a foreign affiliate through inflated management fees, unsupported referral commissions, royalty charges, shareholder costs, interest, guarantees, or non-arm's-length candidate-placement allocations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment to Egyptian taxable income, denial of unsupported deductions, additional tax, interest, documentation penalties, and possible corresponding-adjustment disputes with the foreign jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face personal exposure if they knowingly approved fabricated documentation, sham arrangements, or deliberate tax evasion. Ordinary transfer-pricing disagreement generally creates corporate assessment exposure rather than automatic director imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Egyptian LLC solely as an invoicing conduit while all people, decisions, client negotiations, candidate screening, contract execution, and revenue-generating functions occur abroad, or using nominee arrangements that conceal the real controller.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reallocation of income, denial of deductions, permanent-establishment or beneficial-ownership findings, penalties for inaccurate filings, and potential sham-transaction or tax-evasion prosecution where intent and deception are established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face civil restitution, enforcement against assets, and criminal liability for deliberate concealment or fraudulent arrangements. Travel bans or imprisonment require the relevant statutory and judicial basis and are not automatic consequences of low substance alone.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register for VAT when the statutory threshold or compulsory-registration rule is met, failing to issue compliant electronic invoices, misclassifying taxable recruitment or consulting services, or claiming input VAT without valid supporting documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessment, denial of input-tax credits, late-payment charges, administrative penalties, electronic-invoicing sanctions, and potential criminal consequences for deliberate false invoicing or tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company is ordinarily the primary debtor, but responsible officers and signatories may face personal sanctions where they knowingly issued false invoices, obstructed inspection, or participated in deliberate VAT evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Payroll, social insurance, and employment misclassification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating employees as independent candidates or contractors to avoid payroll withholding or social-insurance obligations, omitting expatriate remuneration, or failing to report taxable benefits and employment-related payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Back payroll tax, social-insurance contributions, penalties, interest, employment-law assessments, and possible sanctions for false payroll records or non-registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible managers may be personally liable for deliberate concealment, false payroll records, or failure to make required deductions. Company-level liability remains primary for ordinary arrears.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, using personal accounts, disguising the beneficial owner, failing to retain customer or payer information, or processing suspicious cross-border funds through recruitment retainers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious-transaction reporting consequences, account restrictions, confiscation or asset-freezing measures, administrative sanctions, and criminal penalties under Egyptian anti-money-laundering legislation for money laundering or related offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, beneficial owners, and employees may face personal criminal liability for knowing participation, facilitation, concealment, or failure to perform legally required controls. Imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and travel restrictions depend on the offense and judicial process.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing recruitment, overseas placement, labor supply, manpower outsourcing, or employment-agency services without the required Egyptian license or outside the licensed scope, particularly where the business presents itself as an executive-search firm but performs regulated labor placement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory closure, license suspension or cancellation, administrative fines, disgorgement or restitution, and possible criminal sanctions under applicable labor and recruitment legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers who knowingly operate without authorization may face personal fines or criminal liability. Corporate limited liability does not protect a person from liability for their own unlawful conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Obstruction of tax inspection or records destruction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Refusing access to books, deleting electronic communications, withholding contracts or bank records, concealing beneficial-owner information, or interfering with an ETA audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Separate administrative or criminal penalties, adverse assessment based on available information, additional tax, and loss of evidentiary credibility.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and any person responsible for obstruction may face personal fines or imprisonment where provided by law. Corporate status does not shield an individual who destroys records or obstructs an investigation.
